rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revealed Book confirms other heavenly scriptures, fulfilling the believers’ confession that they accept what was sent to both communities.
rows.anchor: أنزلناه مصدقا لسائر الكتب السماوية ، تحقيقا لقوله : آمنا بالذي أنزل إلينا وأنزل إليكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God sent Muhammad a Book just as He sent Books to those before him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كما أنزلنا الكتب إلى من كان قبلك أنزلنا إليك الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given the Book are Abdullah ibn Salam and the people who believed with him.
rows.anchor: فالذين ءاتيناهم الكتاب } هم عبد الله بن سلام ومن آمن معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among these” refers to the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: ومن هؤلاء } من أهل مكة وقيل : أراد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the recipients are earlier People of the Book, while “among these” means their contemporaries in the Prophet’s time.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أراد بالذين أوتوا الكتاب الذين تقدموا عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the signs’ clarity and removal of doubt, only those deeply committed to disbelief reject them.
rows.anchor: مع ظهورها وزوال الشبهة عنها ، إلا المتوغلون في الكفر المصممون عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another identification of those who deny the signs is Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and his companions.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هم كعب بن الأشرف وأصحابه

words: وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was unlettered: no one had ever known him to recite a book or write one.
rows.anchor: وأنت أمي ما عرفك أحد قط بتلاوة كتاب ولا خط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If he had read or written, the People of the Book could doubt him, saying he did not match their description of an unlettered prophet.
rows.anchor: من أهل الكتاب وقالوا : الذي نجده في كتبنا أمي لا يكتب ولا يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Meccan polytheists might suspect that Muhammad learned the Qur’an or wrote it himself.
rows.anchor: أو لارتاب مشركو مكة وقالوا : لعله تعلمه أو كتبه بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called falsifiers because they disbelieved despite his illiteracy, which leaves no ground for suspicion; literacy would invite stronger doubts.
rows.anchor: سماهم مبطلين لأنهم كفروا به وهو أمي بعيد من الريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other prophets were not unlettered, yet belief in them was required because God confirmed them through miracles; even supposing Muhammad literate, his opponents should believe by the same proof, especially since the Qur’an is miraculous while earlier scriptures are not.
rows.anchor: سائر الأنبياء عليهم السلام لم يكونوا أميين ، ووجب الإيمان بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the right hand, the instrument of writing, makes the denial that he wrote more vivid, as it would strengthen an affirmation that he wrote a book.
rows.anchor: ذكر اليمين وهي الجارحة التي يزاول بها الخط : زيادة تصوير لما نفى عنه من كونه كاتبا

words: بل هو آيات بينات في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s clear signs are in learned keepers’ hearts; its inimitability, preservation in hearts, and public recitation by most of the community distinguish it from earlier non-miraculous books read from codices.
rows.anchor: وهما من خصائص القرآن : كون آياته بينات الإعجاز ، وكونه محفوظا في الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A description of this community says that their breasts are their Gospels; no authority is named here.
rows.anchor:
هذه الأمة
( 831 ) ( صدورهم أناجيلهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the deeply unjust and obstinately defiant reject God’s manifest signs.
rows.anchor: وما يجحد } بآيات الله الواضحة ، إلا المتوغلون في الظلم المكابرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening waw coordinates with an omitted preceding clause of the same kind as the following clause.
rows.anchor: للعطف على معطوف عليه منوي من جنس المعطوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “to them” refers to the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { لهم } لأهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb “guide” is read with nūn or yāʾ; its agent is understood from the mention of destroyed generations, since “how many” cannot be the subject.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالنون والياء ، والفاعل ما دل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One construction supplies “the great number of Our destroying generations” as subject; another takes the statement itself to guide, like “There is no god but God” protecting lives and property.
rows.anchor: تقديره : أو لم يهد لهم كثرة إهلاكنا القرون . أو هذا الكلام كما هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may also have an implicit subject referring to God, as indicated by the nūn reading.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون فيه ضمير الله بدلالة القراءة والنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroyed generations are ʿĀd, Thamud, and Lot’s people.
rows.anchor: و { القرون } عاد وثمود وقوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans pass through those peoples’ dwellings and lands on trading journeys.
rows.anchor: يعني أهل مكة ، يمرون في متاجرهم على ديارهم وبلادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads “they walk” with a doubled shadda.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يمشون ) بالتشديد

none: The segment contains only the quoted verse text and a heading.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “O mountains” can be apposed to “favor,” or to “We gave” with an implied “Our saying” or “We said.”
rows.anchor: يا جبال } إما أن يكون بدلا من { فضلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two readings are given for “repeat with him,” both derived from taʾwīb.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( أوبي ) و ( أوبي ) من التأويب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aوب means return: the mountains repeat glorification with David or return to it whenever he does, since repetition is itself a return.
rows.anchor: والأوب : أي رجعي معه التسبيح . أو ارجعى معه في التسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates glorification in the mountains as He created speech in the tree; their sound is heard like a glorifier’s, a miracle for David.
rows.anchor: أن الله سبحانه وتعالى يخلق فيها تسبيحا كما خلق الكلام في الشجرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, David lamented his sin with mournful repetition, and mountains echoed him as birds joined their voices.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان ينوح على ذنبه بترجيع وتحزين ، وكانت الجبال تسعده على نوحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “And the birds” is read in the nominative and accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( والطير ) ، رفعا ونصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birds may coordinate with the mountains’ wording or grammatical position, be a comitative object, or coordinate with “favor,” meaning they too were subjected to David.
rows.anchor: وعطفا على لفظ الجبال ومحلها . وجوزوا أن ينتصب مفعولا معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is more majestic than a plain statement that God gave David favor and caused mountains and birds to repeat with him.
rows.anchor: كم بينهما . ألا ترى إلى ما فيه من الفخامة التي لا تخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing mountains as rational beings who obey and answer displays divine lordship and majesty, showing all creatures and inanimate things submit to God’s will.
rows.anchor: حيث جعلت الجبال منزلة منزلة العقلاء الذي إذا أمرهم أطاعوا وأذعنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made iron as soft as clay, dough, or wax for David to shape by hand without fire or hammering.
rows.anchor: وجعلناه له لينا كالطين والعجين والشمع ، يصرفه بيده كيف يشاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says iron was pliable in David’s hand because he had extraordinary strength.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لأن الحديد في يده لما أوتي من شدة القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has ṣābighāt, an accusative plural form.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( صابغات ) وهي الدروع الواسعة الضافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sābighāt are broad coats of mail; David first made them, whereas armor had been plates.
rows.anchor: وهي الدروع الواسعة الضافية ، وهو أول من اتخذها وكانت قبل صفائح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said David sold armor for four thousand, supporting his household while giving alms to the poor.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان يبيع الدرع بأربعة آلاف فينفق منها على نفسه وعياله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A story says David went incognito to ask about himself; an angel praised him except for family support from the treasury, so he asked God for a livelihood and was taught armor-making.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان يخرج حين ملك بني إسرائيل متنكرا ، فيسأل الناس عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Set armor nails to a proper size: thin ones loosen the links, thick ones split them; sard is the weaving of armor.
rows.anchor: لا تجعل المسامير دقاقا فتقلق ، ولا غلاظا فتفصم الحلق . والسرد : نسج الدروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural command to do good is addressed to David and his household.
rows.anchor: { واعملوا } الضمير لدواد وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind clause is construed differently with accusative and nominative readings; “winds” also has a nominative reading.
rows.anchor: فيمن نصب : ولسليمان الريح مسخرة ، فيمن رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind covered a month’s journey in the morning and another in the evening.
rows.anchor: جريها بالغداة مسيرة شهر ، وجريها بالعشي كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads “its morning journey and its evening journey.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( غدوتها وروحتها )

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Solomon’s party traveled in the morning, rested at Istakhr at noon, then traveled in the evening and arrived at Kabul.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن رضي الله عنه : كان يغدون فيقيل باصطخر ، ثم يروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An inscription said to be written by a companion of Solomon at a house near the Tigris describes the party’s journey from Istakhr toward Syria in a day.
rows.anchor: ويحكى أن بعضهم رأي مكتوبا في منزل بناحية دجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qitr means molten copper.
rows.anchor: القطر : النحاس المذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The copper fountain is a mine God melted for Solomon; it flowed like water, so it was named for what it became, as in Joseph’s dream of squeezing wine.
rows.anchor: أراد بها معدن النحاس ولكنه أساله كما ألان الحديد لداود

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says the copper flowed for Solomon three days each month.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان يسبل في الشهر ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “By permission of his Lord” means by His command.
rows.anchor: بإذن ربه } بأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever deviates from God’s command turns from the command to obey Solomon.
rows.anchor: عن أمرنا } الذي أمرناه به من طاعة سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant derives the verb from the causative form azāghahu.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يزغ من أزاغه )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the punishment of the Blaze as the punishment of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says an angel with a whip of fire struck disobedient jinn, though they could not see the angel.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي : كان معه ملك بيده سوط من نار ، كلما استعصى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miḥrābs are lofty protected residences or seats, so called because they are defended; another view says they are mosques.
rows.anchor: المحاريب : المساكن والمجالس الشريفة المصونة عن الابتذال : سميت محاريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The figures were images of angels, prophets, and righteous people, made of brass, copper, glass, or marble for people to see and emulate in worship.
rows.anchor: والتماثيل : صور الملائكة والنبيين والصالحين ، كانت تعمل في المساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Image-making could be lawful under another religious law because it is not intrinsically rationally evil like injustice or lying; Abu al-Aliya says it was not then prohibited.
rows.anchor: هذا مما يجوز أن تختلف في الشرائع لأنه ليس من مقبحات العقل كالظلم والكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, figures could depict nonliving things such as trees, since the term includes any likeness, or they could be headless.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون غير صور الحيوان كصور الأشجار وغيرها ؛ لأن التمثال كل ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says two lions were made below Solomon’s throne and two eagles above it; they helped him ascend and shaded him seated.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهم عملوا له أسدين في أسفل كرسيه ، ونسرين فوقه ، فإذا أراد أن يصعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jawābī are large basins.
rows.anchor: والجوابي : الحياض الكبار ، قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wizr and wiqr are synonyms; the verb means to carry a burden.
rows.anchor: الوزر والوقر : أخوان ؛ ووزر الشيء إذا حمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Resurrection each soul bears its own sin; nobody is punished for another’s, unlike worldly tyrants who punish one for another’s wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أن كل نفس يوم القيامة لا تحمل إلا وزرها الذي اقترفته : لا تؤخذ نفس بذنب نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine “burden-bearing” describes souls themselves: each burdened soul is found carrying its own, never another’s burden.
rows.anchor: لأن المعنى أن النفوس الوازرات لا ترى منهن واحدة إلا حاملة وزرها ، لا وزر غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The misleaders’ additional burdens are their own sins of leading others astray, not other people’s sins.
rows.anchor: تلك الآية في الضالين المضلين ، وأنهم يحملون أثقال إضلال الناس مع أثقال ضلالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God refutes the misleaders’ promise to carry followers’ sins by saying they will carry none of those sins.
rows.anchor: كذبهم الله تعالى في قولهم : { اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم } ( العنكبوت : 12 )

words: وَإِن تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ إِلَىٰ حِمْلِهَا لَا يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَىْءٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause establishes divine justice in not punishing without personal sin; the next says no one relieves a burdened soul who begs for help.
rows.anchor: الأول في الدلالة على عدل الله تعالى في حكمه ، وأنه تعالى لا يؤاخذ نفسا بغير ذنبها ، والثاني : في أن لا غياث يومئذ لمن استغاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a close relative—father, child, or brother—will not answer a burdened soul’s plea to carry part of its load.
rows.anchor: وإن كان المدعو بعض قرابتها من أب أو ولد أو أخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deficient verb’s implied subject is the person summoned, understood from the burdened soul’s call; omitting that person includes every possible summoned person.
rows.anchor: إلى المدعو المفهوم من قوله : { وإن تدع مثقلة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a distributive generalization: not all summoned people can be relatives, but each possible person is covered in turn.
rows.anchor: هو من العموم الكائن على طريق البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads dhū in the nominative and kāna as a complete verb, like the verse about a debtor in hardship.
rows.anchor: ما تقول فيمن قرأ : ( ولو كان ذو قربى ) على كان التامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The incomplete kāna fits better: even if the person called were a relative; the complete verb would disrupt the passage’s cohesion.
rows.anchor: نظم الكلام أحسن ملاءمة للناقصة ؛ لأن المعنى على أن المثقلة إن دعت أحدا إلى حملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In the unseen” can describe people fearing while unseen from punishment, or punishment unseen from them.
rows.anchor: بالغيب } حال من الفاعل أو المفعول ، أي : يخشون ربهم غائبين عن عذابه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes “in the unseen” to mean privately or secretly.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بالغيب في السر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This describes the Prophet’s Companions, who habitually feared God and established prayer as an enduring landmark and raised standard.
rows.anchor: وهذه صفة الذين كانوا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أصحابه ، فكانت عادتهم المستمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet can warn and benefit receptive people, unlike rebellious and obstinate opponents.
rows.anchor: إنما تقدر على إنذار هؤلاء وتحذيرهم من قومك ، وعلى تحصيل منفعة الإنذار فيهم دون متمرديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification means acts of obedience and leaving sins; fear and prayer are part of purification.
rows.anchor: ومن تزكى } ومن تطهر بفعل الطاعات وترك المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads “whoever is more purified, purifies himself.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( من أزكى فإنما يزكي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God promises reward for those who purify themselves.
rows.anchor: وإلى الله المصير } وعد للمتزكين بالثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After threatening opponents with removal, the passage describes the Resurrection’s terrors and then says only certain people benefit from warning; Muhammad may have warned them without effect before God disclosed their condition.
rows.anchor: لما غضب عليهم في قوله : { إن يشأ يذهبكم } أتبعه الإنذار بيوم القيامة وذكر أهوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Muhammad warned of the Resurrection’s terrors without benefit, so God told him who would benefit.
rows.anchor: أو أخبره الله تعالى بعلمه فيهم

none: The segment is a continuation containing only quoted verse text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruit colors may mean kinds such as pomegranates, apples, figs, and grapes, or hues such as red, yellow, and green.
rows.anchor: ألوانها } أجناسها من الرمان والتفاح والتين والعنب وغيرها مما لا يحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judad means stripes, lines, or paths.
rows.anchor: والجدد : الخطط والطرائق . قال لبيد

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid’s line uses judad for marked lines or pathways, supporting this lexical sense.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد : أو مذهب جدد على ألواحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word also describes a dark stripe on a donkey’s back and two dark lines on a gazelle separating its back and belly colors.
rows.anchor: ويقال : جدة الحمار للخطة السوداء على ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gharābīb coordinates with “white” or “judad,” describing striped mountains and mountains of a single color.
rows.anchor: معطوف على بيض أو على جدد ، كأنه قيل : ومن الجبال مخطط ذو جدد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima identifies the gharābīb as tall black mountains.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة رضي الله عنه : هي الجبال الطوال السود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gharīb intensifies blackness, as in “black gharīb” or “black ḥalkūk”; it is associated with the raven and extreme darkness.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : الغربيب تأكيد للأسود . يقال : أسود غربيب ، وأسود حلكوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though emphasis normally follows its noun, “black” is understood before gharīb, which explains it; this intensifies through explicit expression and implication together.
rows.anchor: ومن حق التأكيد أن يتبع المؤكد كقولك : أصفر فاقع ، وأبيض يقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied-and-expressed wording strengthens emphasis by indicating the same meaning explicitly and implicitly.
rows.anchor: إنما يفعل ذلك لزيادة التوكيد ، حيث يدل على المعنى الواحد من طريقي الإظهار والإضمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mountains with stripes” requires an omitted possessive phrase, yielding mountains whose white, red, and black stripes make their colors varied.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من تقدير حذف المضاف في قوله تعالى : { ومن الجبال جدد } بمعنى : ومن الجبال ذو جدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among people, beasts, and livestock, varied in color” means some among them have different colors, like fruits and mountains.
rows.anchor: يعني : ومنهم بعض مختلف ألوانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads alwānuha, “their colors,” in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ألوانها ) ، وقرأ الزهري

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reads judad with ḍamma as the plural of jadīda, “new path,” comparing its pattern to safīna, sufun, safāʾin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري : ( جدد ) ، بالضم : جمع جديدة

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb’s line describing a wild ass uses jadāʾid for paths or ridges.
rows.anchor: وقد فسر بها قول أبي ذؤيب يصف حمار وحش : جون السراة له جدائد اربع

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: A second al-Zuhri reading has judad with two fatḥas, meaning a clear, bright path used for distinct stripes.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه : جدد ، بفتحتين ، وهو الطريق الواضح المسفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant lightens al-dawābb; like al-ḍāllīn, the readings avoid meeting two vowelless consonants, one moving the first and the other deleting the last.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( والدواب ) مخففا ونظير هذا التخفيف قراءة من قرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Likewise” points back to variety in fruits and mountains.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { كذالك } أي كاختلاف الثمرات والجبال

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know God know His attributes, justice, oneness, and what is possible or impossible for Him; they honor and fear Him as He deserves.
rows.anchor: والمراد : العلماء به الذين علموه بصفاته وعدله وتوحيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more one knows God, the more one fears Him; the less one knows Him, the more secure one feels.
rows.anchor: ومن ازداد به علما ازداد منه خوفا ، ومن كان علمه به أقل كان آمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ in “so that they die” answers the negation and is subjunctive with an implicit an.
rows.anchor: فيموتوا } جواب النفي ، ونصبه بإضمار أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads “they die” in the nominative, coordinating it with “judgment is passed” and including it in the negation; compare the verse about not being allowed to speak.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( فيموتون ) عطفا على يقضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Like that” means with that kind of recompense.
rows.anchor: كذالك } مثل ذلك الجزاء { نجزى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage has variants with yujāzā and nujzī; nujzī uses first-person nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يجازى ) . ( ونجزي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaṣṭarikhūn means they cry out intensely; it derives from strenuous shouting and is used for desperate pleas.
rows.anchor: يصطرخون } يتصارخون : يفتعلون من الصراخ وهو الصياح بجهد وشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line compares the sound to a pregnant animal’s cry after its foal has been taken away.
rows.anchor:
قال : 
كصرخة حبلى أسلمتها قبيلها ;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source compares their request to the earlier appeal, “Return us, and we will do righteous deeds.”
rows.anchor: كما أكتفى به في قوله تعالى : { فارجعنا نعمل صالحا } ( السجدة : 12 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added phrase heightens regret and admits prior wrongdoing; it does not imply other good deeds, since they were disbelievers and sinners.
rows.anchor: فائدته زيادة التحسر على ما عملوه من غير الصالح مع الاعتراف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They thought their conduct righteous, as in the verse about people who believe they do good; they ask to do good other than what they mistook for good.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا يحسبون أنهم على سيرة صالحة ، كما قال الله تعالى : { وهم يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Did We not give you a long life?” is God’s reproach, meaning “We will say to them.”
rows.anchor: توبيخ من الله يعني : فنقول لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads mā yudhakkaru fīhi, from adhkara with assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وما يذكر فيه ) من أذكر على الإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning covers every lifespan long enough to correct one’s affairs, even a short one, though reproach is greater for a long life.
rows.anchor: وهو متناول لكل عمر تمكن فيه المكلف من إصلاح شأنه وإن قصر ؛ إلا أن التوبيخ في المتطاول أعظم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the age at which God has given a person sufficient excuse is sixty years.
rows.anchor:
وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :
( 928 ) ( العمر الذي أعذر الله فيه إلى ابن آدم ستون سنة )

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the relevant age as twenty to sixty.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : ما بين العشرين إلى الستين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view sets it at eighteen or seventeen.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ثماني عشر وسبع عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warner is Muhammad, the Messenger.
rows.anchor: { النذير } الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the warner as gray hair.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الشيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads nadhur, “warners,” in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وجاءتكم النذر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause coordinates with the meaning of “Did We not give you a long life?”: although a question in form, it states that God gave them life and a warner came.
rows.anchor: على معنى : أو لم نعمركم ؛ لأن لفظه لفظ استخبار . ومعناه معنى إخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the prior passage denies faith despite warning, it means warning has not achieved its aim, faith; “you warn only” says that aim is reached by followers of the Reminder—Qur’an or exhortation—who fear their Lord.
rows.anchor: وإنما كانت تصح هذه التقفية لو كان الإنذار منفيا . قلت : هو كما قلت ، ولكن لما كان ذلك نفيا للإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reverses development: infancy begins weak and ignorant, maturity brings strength and knowledge, and old age returns people to weakness, diminished reason, and ignorance, like an inverted arrow.
rows.anchor: نقلبه فيه فنخلقه على عكس ما خلقناه من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses about returning to decrepit age and the lowest state describe this reversal from knowledge and strength to ignorance and weakness.
rows.anchor: قال عز وجل : { ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكي لا يعلم * من بعد علم شيئا } ( الحج : 5 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who turns youth and strength to old age and weakness can also blot sight, transform people in place, and do as He wills.
rows.anchor: وهذه دلالة على أن من ينقلهم من الشباب إلى الهرم ومن القوة إلى الضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Variants are reported for nunakkisuhu, with kasra on the kāf and forms from tankīs and inkās.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : بكسر الكاف ( وننكسه ) و ( ننكسه ) من التنكيس والإنكاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final verb is read with yāʾ or tāʾ: “do they not reason?” or “do you not reason?”
rows.anchor: من التنكيس والإنكاس { أفلا يعقلون } بالياء والتاء

rows.speaker: عقبة بن أبي معيط
rows.claim: The source reports that ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt was the person who called the Messenger a poet.
rows.anchor: كانوا يقولون لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : شاعر ، وروي أن القائل : عقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We did not teach him poetry” means God did not teach poetry through the Qur’an: it is not poetry and has no relation to it.
rows.anchor: أي : وما علمناه بتعليم القرآن الشعر ، على معنى : أن القرآن ليس بشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry is metered, rhymed speech pursuing poets’ chosen meanings; the Qur’an lacks its meter, rhyme, themes, arrangement, and styles.
rows.anchor: والشعر إنما هو كلام موزون مقفى ، يدل على معنى ، فأين الوزن ؟ وأين التقفية ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It was neither fitting nor possible for Muhammad to compose poetry: even if he tried, it would not come easily, just as he could not write, strengthening proof and dispelling doubt.
rows.anchor: وما يصح له ولا يتطلب لو طلبه ، أي : جعلناه بحيث لو أراد قرض الشعر لم يتأت له

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says poetry was dearer to the Messenger than much speech, but did not come readily to him.
rows.anchor: وعن الخليل : كان الشعر أحب إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كثير من الكلام ، ولكن كان لا يتأتى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s “I am the prophet, no lie” and “bloodied finger” lines are natural, uncrafted speech, not deliberate poetry; accidental meter in ordinary speech is not called poetry.
rows.anchor: أنا النبي لا كذب … أنا ابن عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil did not count truncated rajaz as poetry, answering the objection from the Prophet’s metrical phrases.
rows.anchor: على أن الخليل ما كان يعد المشطور من الرجز شعرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a reminder from God to admonish humans and jinn, and a heavenly Book recited in worship whose recitation and practice bring success, unlike poetry inspired by devils.
rows.anchor: يعني : ما هو إلا ذكر من الله تعالى يوعظ به الإنس والجن ، كما قال : { إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of “that he may warn” may be the Qur’an or the Messenger.
rows.anchor: لينذر } القرآن أو الرسول وقرىء : ( لتنذر ) بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads li-tundhira in the second person, addressing the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( لتنذر ) بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb nadhara bihi can mean to know or become informed of something.
rows.anchor: ولينذر : من نذر به إذا علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The living person reasons, since the heedless are like the dead; alternatively, it means one known to believe and live by faith.
rows.anchor: أي عاقلا متأملا ، لأن الغافل كالميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement of punishment becomes binding on disbelievers who do not reflect and are not expected to believe.
rows.anchor: وتجب كلمة العذاب { على الكافرين } الذي لا يتأملون ولا يتوقع منهم الإيمان

none: The segment contains only quoted verse text, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other layers of fire beneath them are canopies for others; this punishment threatens and frightens God’s servants so they avoid it.
rows.anchor: ومن تحتهم } أطباق من النار هي { ظلل } لآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads “O My servants” in the vocative.
rows.anchor: وهذه عظة من الله تعالى ونصيحة بالغة . وقرىء : ( يا عبادي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fear Me” warns them not to do what incurs God’s displeasure; this is a solemn admonition and sincere counsel.
rows.anchor: ولا تتعرضوا لما يوجب سخطي ، وهذه عظة من الله تعالى ونصيحة بالغة
